title: Cognitive and Behavioral Development of 9-Year-Old Children After Maternal Cancer During Pregnancy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
ehr_evidence: A neuropsychologic examination, assessing intelligence quotient, attention, memory, and behavior, was performed... parents completed a questionnaire on their child's general health and educational level. All tests were conducted in the child's native language.
summary: A cross-sectional analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of 151 nine-year-old children prenatally exposed to maternal cancer and its treatment, assessing cognitive and behavioral outcomes.
key_findings: Mean cognitive and behavioral outcomes were within normal ranges with no difference in FSIQ between treatment types (F[4,140] = 0.45, P = .776) or cancer stages (F[3,140] = 1.53, P = .211).
Gestational age at birth showed a positive association with FSIQ, increasing by 1.6 points (95% CI, 0.7 to 2.5; P < .001) for each week increase in gestational age.
No associations were found between FSIQ and chemotherapeutic agent, exposure level, or timing during pregnancy in children prenatally exposed to chemotherapy (all P > .08).

Maternal bereavement had an effect on FSIQ (F[2, 144] = 3.94, P = .022) with lower FSIQ in children with a deceased mother before age 2 years (93.13 ± 12.65) than with a surviving mother (104.08 ± 14.88), but this association disappeared after adjusting for gestational age (P > .3).

In multiple linear regression, gestational age (P = .006) and maternal education level (P = .005) remained significant predictors of FSIQ, estimating an increase of 1.27 points (± 0.45) per week increase in GA.
In the chemotherapy subgroup, only maternal education level remained a significant predictor of FSIQ (P = .011).

A significant relation was found between maternal bereavement before age 2 years and remedial care (χ2 [2,127] = 7.33, P = .026, φ = 0.240), and between remedial support and prematurity (24 children, 77.4% born preterm; χ2 [1,127] = 6.67, P = .010, φ = 0.229).
study_design: Cross-sectional analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort
population: 151 nine-year-old children (mean age 9.3 years, range 7.8-10.6 years) prenatally exposed to maternal cancer, from Belgium, Netherlands, Italy, Czech Republic, and New Jersey
exposure_domain: Maternal cancer during pregnancy and its treatment (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy, trastuzumab)
limitations: Underpowered analysis in the smaller chemotherapy subgroup, possibly masking a prematurity effect.
Multicollinearity/multicollinearity between maternal death and premature birth makes disentangling effects difficult.
Remedial support rates cannot be compared with the general population because general population rates are under-reported.
Small sample size for maternal bereavement analysis requires larger studies.
